label: def:double-slit-q-phase
title: $q$-deformed path phase
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q \in k^{\times} (substrate parameter), and let \gamma_i (i = 1,2) be two paths through slits of width a separated by distance d.

For a massive excitation of rest mass m, the spatial wavelength is not an external optical parameter; it is forced by Lorentz covariance of the internal meridian clock. In its rest frame, the excitation ticks at the Compton angular frequency \omega_0 = m c^2 / \hbar of the exceptional-divisor meridian cycle (meridian Compton tick). Following Louis de Broglie (1924), boosting along the beam axis at velocity v with Lorentz factor \gamma^2(1 - v^2 / c^2) = 1 transforms proper time as \tau_{\mathrm{prop}} = \gamma(t - v x / c^2) and decomposes the invariant clock phase into temporal and spatial components:

  \omega_0 \tau_{\mathrm{prop}}
  = \frac{E t - p x}{\hbar},
  \qquad
  E = \gamma m c^2,
  \qquad
  p = \gamma m v,
  \qquad
  E^2 - (p c)^2 = (m c^2)^2.

The spatial gradient fixes the relativistic de Broglie wavenumber k_{\mathrm{dB}} = p / \hbar and wavelength \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} = 2\pi\hbar / p = h / (\gamma m v), with phase velocity E / p satisfying (E / p)\,v = c^2.

Along each slit trajectory \gamma_i, the q-exterior derivative d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d splits the accumulated q-deformed path phase into horizontal and vertical parts:

  \Phi_q^{(i)}(y)
  = \frac{1}{\hbar_q}\!\int_{\gamma_i}\! d_q\psi
  = q^{-1}\Phi_{\mathrm{geom}}^{(i)}(y)
      + (1 - q^{-1})\Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(i)}(y),

where:

  • \Phi_{\mathrm{geom}}^{(i)}(y) = (2\pi / \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}})\,\ell_i(y) is the horizontal de Broglie geometric phase along path length \ell_i(y),
  • \Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(i)}(y) = \int_{\gamma_i} \iota_\xi\varTheta is the vertical Reeb phase, and
  • \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} is the quantum Planck constant.

Subtracting the two paths at scattering angle \theta gives the q-deformed interference phase difference

  \Delta\Phi_q(y)
  = \Phi_q^{(1)}(y) - \Phi_q^{(2)}(y)
  = q^{-1}\frac{2\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}}
      + (1 - q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi(y)
  = \frac{2\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda_q}
      + (1 - q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi(y),

where \Delta\phi_\xi(y) is the Reeb phase mismatch and \lambda_q = q\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} is the stretched effective fringe wavelength. At detector distance L, the horizontal q^{-1} factor stretches the Young fringe spacing to \Delta y_q = q\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} L / d, whereas the q^{-2}\Delta classical Hodge core of the q-Laplacian expansion broadens the single-slit diffraction envelope by q^2 for controlled comparison with relativistic 600\;\mathrm{eV} electron interferometry [bach2013]. At q = 1, the Reeb mismatch vanishes and \lambda_q reduces to \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}.
